after: ## Where this fits in the syllabus
alt: Identities centres on personal and cultural experience; Sharing the planet on issues and debate. So three structures matter more: opinion (express and justify a position), cause and effect (because of, as a result, this leads to) and comparison (more or less, similarity or difference). A chain shows a change in one country's economy affecting another.
caption: Opinion, cause-and-effect and comparison language matter more on this theme.

alt: Sharing the planet explores the challenges and opportunities faced by individuals and communities in the modern world. A central circle links its seven recommended topics, each with the language it needs: the environment (opinion), human rights (formal register), peace and conflict, equality (comparison), globalization (cause and effect), ethics (justifying a position) and urban and rural environments (comparing settings and change).
caption: Seven topics, each with its own language focus: revise all seven, not one or two.

after: ## Worked example: preparing one topic across all four skills
alt: Globalization at the centre is linked to four kinds of preparation: vocabulary (cause-and-effect connectives), reading and listening (unseen news-style texts about consequences across borders), writing (a formal article or report arguing a position) and speaking (discussing a globalization image, or at HL a literary work).
caption: One topic, four skills: revision that transfers to any paper.

after: ## Preparing Paper 1's writing task for this theme
alt: Three text-type categories with examples: personal (a blog post), professional (a formal letter, a report) and mass media (an article), with professional and mass media highlighted as often suiting this issue-driven theme. An arrow leads from reviewing vocabulary only to practising an opinion article or formal letter in the real conventions.
caption: Practise formal, argument-structured text types in their real conventions.

alt: A table pairs four mistakes with fixes: revise all seven topics, not one or two; give listening and reading real time because they carry 50 percent; use opinion, comparison and cause-and-effect language instead of description; and build comprehension of authentic issue-driven texts as well as formal writing.
caption: Cover all seven topics, practise comprehension, and use issues language.
